book: The Art of Game Design: A Book of Lenses (Jesse Schell, 2008)
goal: The user reads at a limited pace; the agent provides comprehensive reading support so the user understands each chapter fully before moving on.
reading_method: Extract the full chapter from the PDF. Map structure + ideas (not 1:1 verbatim): follow the book's section order; keep every major claim, key example, and lens; drop flourish. Write notes.md in English on that skeleton. In chat, deliver the same skeleton in Vietnamese: (1) core argument, (2) key ideas with the book's examples, (3) that chapter's Lenses as question checklists, (4) a link to earlier chapters, (5) a short comprehension check. A chapter stays in-progress until the user confirms understanding.

conventions.pages: Book page numbers (not PDF page numbers).
conventions.lenses: Lens numbers introduced in that chapter (100 total across the book).
conventions.sequential: Each feature depends on the previous one; read in order.

features.name: Orientation: how to use the book (two tables + Hello)
features.description: Understand the difference between the Table of Contents (lecture path) and the Table of Lenses (toolbox of 100 perspectives), and Schell's reading advice in 'Hello'. Establishes how we will use lenses as question checklists throughout.
features.evidence: notes.md — Front matter: two indexes, acknowledgments, Hello. User moved on to Ch 1–2.

features.name: Ch 1 - In the Beginning, There Is the Designer
features.description: What skills a game designer needs; why listening is the most important skill; the five kinds of listening (team, audience, game, client, self).
features.evidence: notes.md — Chapter 1: identity, failure, listening, five targets, major vs minor gift. User confirmed by continuing to Ch 2.

features.name: Ch 2 - The Designer Creates an Experience
features.description: The game is not the experience; introspection (powers and perils); Essential Experience. Lens #1 Essential Experience.
features.evidence: notes.md — Chapter 2: game ≠ experience; introspection; Essential Experience; Lens #1. User confirmed understanding.

features.name: Ch 3 - The Experience Rises Out of a Game
features.description: Defining 'game'; problem solving as the core. Lenses #2 Surprise, #3 Fun, #4 Curiosity, #5 Endogenous Value, #6 Problem Solving.
features.evidence: notes.md — Chapter 3: definitions; fun/play/game; Lenses #2–#6. User confirmed understanding after a second pass on the author's intent.

features.name: Ch 4 - The Game Consists of Elements
features.description: The Elemental Tetrad: mechanics, story, aesthetics, technology; skin vs skeleton. Lenses #7 Elemental Tetrad, #8 Holographic Design.
features.evidence: notes.md — Chapter 4: elemental tetrad; Space Invaders; skin vs skeleton; Lenses #7–#8. User confirmed understanding.

features.name: Ch 5 - The Elements Support a Theme
features.description: Unifying themes and resonance to make elements reinforce one meaning. Lenses #9 Unification, #10 Resonance.
features.evidence: notes.md — Chapter 5: unifying vs resonant themes; Pirates / Titanic / Toontown; Lenses #9–#10. User confirmed understanding.

features.name: Ch 6 - The Game Begins with an Idea
features.description: Inspiration, stating the problem, and brainstorming tips. Lenses #11 Infinite Inspiration, #12 Problem Statement.
features.evidence: notes.md — Chapter 6: inspiration; problem statement; subconscious; brainstorming tips; Lenses #11–#12. User confirmed understanding.

features.name: Ch 7 - The Game Improves Through Iteration
features.description: The Eight Filters, the Rule of the Loop, risk assessment and rapid prototyping. Lenses #13 Eight Filters, #14 Risk Mitigation, #15 The Toy.
features.evidence: notes.md — Chapter 7: eight filters; Rule of the Loop; risk/prototyping; Lens of the Toy; Lenses #13–#15. User confirmed understanding.

features.name: Ch 8 - The Game Is Made for a Player
features.description: Knowing your audience: demographics and psychographics (player types). Lenses #16 The Player, #17 Pleasure.
features.evidence: notes.md — Chapter 8: audience; age/gender; LeBlanc/Bartle pleasures; Pirates family play; Lenses #16–#17. User confirmed understanding.

features.name: Ch 9 - The Experience Is in the Player's Mind
features.description: Modeling, focus, empathy, imagination, motivation, judgment; flow. Lenses #18 Flow, #19 Needs, #20 Judgment.
features.evidence: notes.md — Chapter 9: modeling; flow; empathy; imagination; Maslow; judgment; Lenses #18–#20. Awaiting user confirmation.

features.name: Ch 10 - Some Elements Are Game Mechanics
features.description: The six mechanics: space, objects/attributes/states, actions, rules, skill, chance. Lenses #21 Functional Space, #22 Dynamic State, #23 Emergence, #24 Action, #25 Goals, #26 Rules, #27 Skill, #28 Expected Value, #29 Chance.

features.name: Ch 11 - Game Mechanics Must Be in Balance
features.description: Twelve types of game balance, balancing economies, dynamic balancing. Lenses #30 Fairness through #47 Balance (18 lenses).

features.name: Ch 12 - Game Mechanics Support Puzzles
features.description: What makes a good puzzle; principles of puzzle design. Lenses #48 Accessibility, #49 Visible Progress, #50 Parallelism, #51 The Pyramid, #52 The Puzzle.

features.name: Ch 13 - Players Play Games Through an Interface
features.description: The loop of interaction, channels of information, juiciness. Lenses #53 Control, #54 Physical Interface, #55 Virtual Interface, #56 Transparency, #57 Feedback, #58 Juiciness, #59 Channels and Dimensions, #60 Modes.

features.name: Ch 14 - Experiences Can Be Judged by Their Interest Curves
features.description: Interest curves and what comprises interest. Lenses #61 Interest Curve, #62 Inherent Interest, #63 Beauty, #64 Projection.

features.name: Ch 15 - One Kind of Experience Is the Story
features.description: Story/game duality, the myth of passive entertainment, story tips. Lenses #65 Story Machine, #66 Obstacle, #67 Simplicity and Transcendence, #68 Hero's Journey, #69 Weirdest Thing, #70 Story.

features.name: Ch 16 - Story and Game Merged with Indirect Control
features.description: The feeling of freedom; six methods of indirect control; collusion. Lenses #71 Freedom, #72 Indirect Control, #73 Collusion.

features.name: Ch 17 - Stories and Games Take Place in Worlds
features.description: Transmedia worlds and what makes them succeed. Lens #74 The World.

features.name: Ch 18 - Worlds Contain Characters
features.description: The nature of game characters, avatars, and creating compelling characters. Lenses #75 Avatar, #76 Character Function, #77 Character Traits, #78 Interpersonal Circumplex, #79 Character Web, #80 Status, #81 Character Transformation.

features.name: Ch 19 - Worlds Contain Spaces
features.description: Architecture and level design; organizing game space. Lenses #82 Inner Contradiction, #83 The Nameless Quality.

features.name: Ch 20 - The Look and Feel Is Defined by Aesthetics
features.description: The value of aesthetics, learning to see, using audio, balancing art and technology. Revisits Lens #63 Beauty.

features.name: Ch 21 - Some Games Are Played with Other Players
features.description: Why we play with others; the social dimension of play.

features.name: Ch 22 - Other Players Sometimes Form Communities
features.description: Building strong communities and dealing with griefing. Lenses #84 Friendship, #85 Expression, #86 Community, #87 Griefing.

features.name: Ch 23 - The Designer Usually Works with a Team
features.description: The secret of successful teamwork; designing together; team communication. Lenses #88 Love, #89 The Team.

features.name: Ch 24 - The Team Communicates Through Documents
features.description: The myth of the game design document; purposes and types of documents. Lens #90 Documentation.

features.name: Ch 25 - Good Games Are Created Through Playtesting
features.description: The five playtest questions (why, who, where, what, how). Lens #91 Playtesting.

features.name: Ch 26 - The Team Builds a Game with Technology
features.description: Foundational vs decorational technology, the hype cycle, the innovator's dilemma. Lenses #92 Technology, #93 Crystal Ball.

features.name: Ch 27 - Your Game Will Probably Have a Client
features.description: Understanding what the client really wants; the three layers of desire. Lens #94 The Client.

features.name: Ch 28 - The Designer Gives the Client a Pitch
features.description: The negotiation of power, hierarchy of ideas, twelve tips for a successful pitch. Lens #95 The Pitch.

features.name: Ch 29 - The Designer and Client Want a Profit
features.description: Business models, units sold, breakeven, learning the language of business. Lens #96 Profit.

features.name: Ch 30 - Games Transform Their Players
features.description: How games change us; can games be good or bad for you. Lens #97 Transformation.

features.name: Ch 31 - Designers Have Certain Responsibilities
features.description: The danger of obscurity, being accountable, your hidden agenda. Lens #98 Responsibility.

features.name: Ch 32 - Each Designer Has a Motivation
features.description: The deepest theming; finding your secret purpose. Lenses #99 The Raven, #100 Your Secret Purpose.

features.name: Ch 33 - Goodbye
features.description: Closing thoughts: 'All Good Things...' and how to keep growing as a designer.

features.name: Synthesis: the 100 lenses as a working toolkit
features.description: After finishing the book, consolidate the 100 lenses into a personal quick-reference and map which lenses matter most for the reader's own goals. Confirm the whole book is understood.
